A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of repeat-detection mechanisms in ESM-3 and ESM-C. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original repeat-prediction accuracies, circuit-discovery experiments, counterfactual comparisons, and attention-head and neuron analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds failure-analysis results, controlled mutation experiments, and neuron-level counterfactual robustness measurements.

M1.justification: The documented neuron-matching procedure replaces the IMGT uncharged concept in v1 Table 13 with polar uncharged amino acids {S,T,N,Q,Y} in v3 Table 14. This is a limited revision to concept selection; the PLMs, circuit-discovery pipeline, clustering, and AUROC assignment procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether existing neuron results were recomputed.

E1.justification: V3 adds a controlled divergence scenario that progressively mutates a repeat while preserving the residue aligned with the masked position, unlike the earlier source-repeat corruption tests. It removes the unrestricted random-protein prediction reference set. The principal synthetic, natural identical, approximate, and indel repeat coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V3 Appendix G.4 newly compares permutation-based discovery with BLOSUM-based discovery for neuron recovery. V1 already compared these counterfactuals for component-level circuits, but its neuron-discovery analysis used BLOSUM counterfactuals only. The existing model comparisons and randomized concept baseline are retained.

E3.justification: New Appendix E introduces accuracy stratification by repeat length and substitution rate, plus a mutation experiment using 40 examples at each repeat length of 10, 20, and 30 residues. It measures induction-head AP-IG attribution while preserving the aligned answer residue. Main model configurations and discovery/evaluation splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds substantial diagnostics of short, divergent repeat failures and tests how induction-head contributions deteriorate under increasing mutation. Appendix G.4 additionally tests whether neuron-level biological findings depend on BLOSUM counterfactuals. These extend v1's component-level robustness studies to mechanism failure and neuron-level sensitivity.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed circuit experiments, variability summaries, and Welch ANOVA for cluster features with p < 0.01. V3's added statistical-test cross-reference points to analysis already present in v1. The new experiments introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: V3 adds Table 4's binned accuracies, Figure 10's attribution trends, and neuron-recovery rates of 83.29% overall and 73.5% for biological-concept neurons in G.4. For example, Table 4 reports 45% and 51% accuracy for ESM-3 and ESM-C on 1–10-residue repeats with 25–50% substitutions. V1's approximately 30% random-protein reference is removed. Table 1 and retained circuit results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The binary neuron concept in the concept-definition table is narrowed from IMGT uncharged to the intersection of uncharged and polar classes, explicitly {S,T,N,Q,Y}. Other mathematical definitions, including faithfulness, attention-head features, gated-MLP equations, and signed AUROC, are retained. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: approximate-repeat circuits subsume exact-repeat functionality, induction mechanisms combine with biological components, and ESM-3 and ESM-C share mechanisms with specific differences. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 interprets declining induction-head attribution as a possible explanation for failures on short, divergent repeats. It also interprets permutation-based neuron recovery as evidence against BLOSUM-specific biological findings. These add substantive qualifications and support while retaining the original mechanism interpretation and coverage limitations.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly documents averaging importance scores over 500 input–counterfactual pairs and scaling aggregated edge scores by 1000 in H.2 and H.5. It supplies sampling and mutation instructions for the new experiment. These clarify documentation without establishing changes to existing experiments; code and data access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Zhang et al. (2026), Controlling Repetition in Protein Language Models, and connects the study's mechanistic findings to concurrent work on pathological generation and steering. The remaining research positioning is retained; other reference edits primarily concern bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and structural edits, including corrected Figure 4 panel references, explanation of faithfulness endpoints, standardized headings, author and publication-header updates, and insertion of the failure-analysis appendix. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 4 and the two-panel Figure 10, revises Figure 6's colors, bar styling, and legend, and reflows later appendix material. Existing tables and figures are largely retained under new numbering rather than replaced; the overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new failure analysis and neuron-level permutation check strengthen the applicability boundaries and empirical support of the mechanistic interpretation. Documentation clarifications also help reproducibility. These targeted gains outweigh the loss of the auxiliary random-protein accuracy reference, but remain limited: the new diagnostics lack uncertainty estimates and do not resolve the study's broader coverage limitations.
